input.prompt:
3D highly rendered animation, soft 3D CGI look. Exactly three characters in the frame: Barnaby, Hazel and Anne. Only one Barnaby is in the frame. Subtitle-free, no logo, no watermark.

REFERENCES: @Image 1 gives Barnaby's head, antlers and colours and @Image 5 gives his full body in profile facing right; @Image 2 gives Hazel; @Image 3 gives Anne, full body; @Image 4 is the location. Every Barnaby reference gives identity only, never size or crop: Barnaby stays at about 45 to 55 percent of the frame height, full antlers inside the frame with clear headroom.

CHARACTERS: Barnaby: chubby moose upright on his two hind legs like a person, red knit sweater with ribbed cuffs; antlers dark chocolate-brown, slightly darker than his fur, about 1.8 times his head width, short round prongs; giant round matte anthracite nose about half as wide as his face, short thick caramel-brown muzzle ending right behind the nose, big round amber-copper eyes, thick brown brows. Hazel: tiny chibi chipmunk, round head about 45 percent of her body, one dark chocolate forehead stripe, flat mint scarf, bushy S-curved tail that stays a big bushy S-curve the whole time, plump cream cheeks, two very big glossy solid black eyes. Anne: moose mother upright like a person, no antlers, smooth round head, big round ears, dark chocolate-brown fur with a cream belly, amber irises, thick mustard-yellow knit shawl without fringe tied at her chest; blunt face-coloured muzzle, giant round matte anthracite nose. FORBIDDEN: any tail, tuft or tail-like bump on Barnaby; a small or shiny nose on Barnaby; white eye-whites on Hazel; antlers or buds on Anne; human fingers on any character; a second Barnaby; Baba or any other moose.

LIGHT: silver full moon gives a thin cool rim light from the upper back; four paper lanterns give one soft, even, constant golden light that warms the faces. Barnaby's fur stays warm caramel-brown and his sweater deep red, Baba's sweater forest green, Anne's shawl mustard-yellow; the night is deep blue, never black.

SUBJECT & ACTION: side view. Barnaby stands at the left of the picture in profile, facing the picture-right; Hazel sits on his shoulder nearest the camera, leaning back, one small smooth capless hazelnut clasped to her chest, never touching Anne. A red maple leaf is already stuck to the red sleeve of his near arm with an amber syrup smear, already there from the very first moment; it stays in the same place for the whole clip. Anne walks in from the right.
Seconds 0 to 1.5: Anne walks to him from the right of the picture, facing left, upright, her shawl swaying, in four brisk steps until her face is close to his, her eyes wide open with the golden glow of the lanterns in them, and she stops.
At second 1.5 Barnaby shuts his eyes and sniffs twice, quick and deep, taking in the warm scent of wool and cinnamon from her mustard shawl right in front of his nose. At about second 2.5 the tip of his nose wiggles up and down twice, quick and springy, on its own, his eyes still shut.
At about second 4.0 the tip of Anne's nose wiggles up and down twice in exactly the same quick springy way; her eyes fill with tears and she whispers, her lips moving to the words, '...Barnaby?' At about second 4.6 Barnaby's eyes open, locked on her face. At about second 5.2 his voice cracks as he answers, his lips moving to the word, 'Mama.'
From about second 6.0 they lean forward and touch noses gently; he tilts his antlers up and back, well above and behind Anne's head, touching nothing; both close their eyes and hold still to the end. Barnaby's antlers stay on his head the whole time. He keeps his back straight and tall and never drops onto four legs.

SCENE: four round white paper lanterns hang still on one twine rope above the table, from the top of the tall wooden bell pole on the right to the maples on the left; a long wooden table with a golden pie, a bowl of cranberries, two corn cobs and a loaf of bread, nobody sitting, no chairs, benches or stools; a brass bell on a bracket on the bell pole at the right end of the table with one short braided cord hanging straight down, already there from the very first moment; a moonlit meadow of red and burgundy maples and fallen red leaves, a deep blue sky, no snow.

CAMERA: a steady side-on medium shot of both in profile, Barnaby about 45 percent of the frame height, single continuous take from second 0 to 8.0, no cut. One slow smooth push-in from second 1.5 to second 6.0, then the camera holds: Barnaby grows from about 45 to at most 55 percent of the frame height and never gets bigger. Barnaby's full antlers stay inside the frame with clear headroom above them the whole shot, at least 25 percent of the frame height above the antler tips.

SOUND: only natural on-set sounds: a dry night breeze, soft hoof steps in dry leaves from 0 to 1.5 only, a faint fabric rustle, two quick small sniffs between 1.5 and 2.2, a tiny soft nose-touch at 6.0, each word heard once, Barnaby warm young male voice, Hazel tiny bright girl voice, Anne warm motherly voice, Baba warm low father voice, one line at a time.
